newsitem.title: UK: Property shortage squeezes UK housing market - RICS.
newsitem.headline: Property shortage squeezes UK housing market - RICS.

text.p: The number of properties for sale in England and Wales has fallen to an eight year low, the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) said in its latest survey.

"The scarcity of properties is forcing up prices but it also means reasonably priced, desirable properties are being sold extremely quickly, giving the false impression that a "boom' is imminent," said RICS housing market spokesman Ian Perry.
A net balance of 43 percent of chartered surveyors reported rising residential property prices in the three months ending September 30, versus the previous three months.
The RICS survey said the number of properties for sale across the country was one third lower during the period compared with the previous three months and at its lowest since December 1988.
"One of the main reasons for homeowners' reluctance to put their properties on the market is their, sometimes over optimistic, expectation of further price rises," said the survey.

It added the promise of payouts by building societies next year as they become banks, combined with expected tax cuts, would encourage homeowners to move after the New Year, leading to a moderation in house prices.
